chunks: (Thereafter Amīr al-mu’minīn alighted from the pulpit)

key_terms.الْمِنْبَرِ: the pulpit or raised platform used for public sermons and addresses
key_terms.عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: peace be upon him, an honorific used for the Imams

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali do after finishing his speech on the minbar?
ai.summary: This concise action marks the formal conclusion of Imam Ali’s (AS) public address during the critical period of the Siffin conflict, where his forces were eventually overpowered by Muawiya’s army. In Shia historiography, this moment underscores the transition from verbal exhortation to the inevitable political and military realities that led to the arbitration (Hukm). The brevity of the narration highlights the gravity of the situation, emphasizing the Imam’s dignified composure amidst growing internal dissent and external pressure.
